format.definition:
start: pragma_source | plain_source
pragma_source: PRAGMA_LINE NEWLINE SOURCE
plain_source: SOURCE

PRAGMA_LINE: /[ \t]*\/\/ @exec:[^\r\n]*/
NEWLINE: /\r?\n/
SOURCE: /[\s\S]+/

tools.name: exec

tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.
tools.name: wait

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

tools.description: Request user input for one to three short questions and wait for the response. This tool is only available in Plan mode.
tools.name: request_user_input

questions.description: Questions to show the user. Prefer 1 and do not exceed 3

header.description: Short header label shown in the UI (12 or fewer chars).

options.description: Provide 2-3 mutually exclusive choices. Put the recommended option first and suffix its label with "(Recommended)". Do not include an "Other" option in this list; the client will add a free-form "Other" option automatically.

description.description: One short sentence explaining impact/tradeoff if selected.

question.description: Single-sentence prompt shown to the user.

tools.description: Tools for reading and waiting on time.
tools.name: clock

tools.description: Pause execution for a specified duration. The sleep ends early when new input arrives for the active turn. Returns the elapsed wall-clock time.
tools.name: sleep

duration_ms.description: How long to sleep in milliseconds. Must be between 1 and 43200000.

tools.description: Tools for spawning and managing sub-agents.
tools.name: collaboration

tools.description: Send a follow-up task to an existing non-root target agent and trigger a turn if it is idle. If the target is already running, deliver the task promptly at message boundaries while sampling, or after the pending tool call completes.
tools.name: followup_task

message.description: Message text to send to the target agent.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to send a follow-up task to (from spawn_agent).

tools.description: Interrupt an agent's current turn, if any, and return its previous status. The agent remains available for messages and follow-up tasks.
tools.name: interrupt_agent

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to interrupt (from spawn_agent).

tools.description: List live agents in the current root thread tree. Optionally filter by task-path prefix.
tools.name: list_agents

path_prefix.description: Task-path prefix filter without a trailing slash. Omit to list all live agents.

tools.description: Send a message to an existing agent. The message will be delivered promptly. Does not trigger a new turn.
tools.name: send_message

message.description: Message text to queue on the target agent.

target.description: Relative or canonical task name to message (from spawn_agent).

tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `gpt-6.1-sol`: Latest workhorse model for coding and everyday work. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-astra`: Frontier intelligence for the most demanding work. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-sol`: Previous generation workhorse model. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-luna`: Fast and affordable model for easier tasks. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-5.6-sol`: Older generation workhorse model. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.
You are then able to refer to this agent as `task_3` or `/root/task1/task_3` interchangeably. However an agent `/root/task2/task_3` would only be able to communicate with this agent via its canonical name `/root/task1/task_3`.
The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.
tools.name: spawn_agent

fork_turns.description: Parent history to inherit. Defaults to `all`; use `none` to start without parent history. Only `all` and `none` are supported.

message.description: Initial plain-text task for the new agent.

model.description: Model override for the new agent. Omit unless an explicit override is needed.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort override for the new agent. Omit to inherit the parent effort.

task_name.description: Task name for the new agent. Use lowercase letters, digits, and underscores.

tools.description: Wait for a mailbox update from any live agent, including queued messages and final-status notifications. The wait also ends early when new user input is steered into the active turn. Does not return the content; returns either a summary of which agents have updates (if any), an interruption summary for steered input, or a timeout summary if no activity arrives before the deadline.
tools.name: wait_agent

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000, min 10000, max 3600000.

tools.description: UI automation through cua_repl using the initialized cua API.
tools.name: mcp__cua_repl

tools.description:
Control native apps or browsers on the user’s computer by reading or operating UI. Prefer purpose-built skills, connectors, APIs, or CLIs when available.

On the first invocation of `cua_repl`, or after resetting it, execute exactly one of the API calls shown below, optionally assigning its result to a variable. Do not add other API calls, waits, or snapshots to that invocation.
The tool result will include documentation and, when creating or selecting a tab or selecting an app, its initial UI state. Selecting a browser does not open a tab. Read that result before continuing.
Use only APIs described in the tool instructions or returned documentation.

When you need an inventory of available apps, browsers, and tabs, get a snapshot of all enabled surfaces. Otherwise, use the relevant entry point below:

```javascript
await cua.getState();
```

Use the first matching browser control option from the user's request:

For a tab @-mention (`mention=tab-v1`):
Pass the complete `plugin://...` URL to get the referenced tab.

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab({ mention: tabMentionUrl });
```

For an existing tab identified by URL in browser context (including the current IAB tab):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab({ url }, { browser: browserId });
```

Known tab ID (`tabId` or `providerTabId`) and browser (name or browser @-mention):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab(tabId, { browser: browserId });
```

To open a URL in the in-app browser (`@Browser`):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.createBrowserTab("iab", url, { visible: boolean });
```

To open a URL in another named browser: pass its name directly; do not call `getBrowser` first.

```javascript
let tab = await cua.createBrowserTab(browserName, url, browserOptions);
```

Known URL, only when the user has not specified a browser by name or @-mention:

```javascript
let browser = await cua.getBrowser({ url });
```

Browser IDs and options:

- `"mcpapps"`: use `cua.getBrowser({ id: "mcpapps" })` for existing full-screen MCP Apps in the task’s side panel.
- `"iab"` (in-app browser): in `createBrowserTab`, use `visible: true` to show the browser; `false` to keep it hidden.
- `"dot"` (Dot): use only when present in browser inventory. It accesses tabs on Dot's active main thread. `cua.getTab(tabId, { browser: "dot" })` selects an existing tab. `cua.createBrowserTab("dot", url, { visible: boolean })` creates one with the same visibility options as `"iab"`.
- `"chrome"` (@Chrome), `"edge"` (@Edge): pass a short, emoji-prefixed `sessionName` (e.g. `"🔎 Task"`) to `createBrowserTab` when starting a task.

On Windows, choose the requested window by app and title from the inventory. Pass the selected window's ID as returned.

```javascript
let app = await cua.getApp({ windowId: selected.id });
```

To add other content to the tool result, use `nodeRepl.write(value)` for text or other values and `await nodeRepl.emitImage(image)` for images. The APIs listed above already display their documentation or UI state; do not wrap their results in `write` or `emitImage`.

If your context begins with a summary of an existing computer use task, call `await cua.rewriteDocumentation()` before continuing the computer use task to ensure you have a complete view of the necessary documentation.

Several `cua_repl.js` calls may work toward the same goal. As soon as you observe the final outcome of the CUA part of the task, make your next tool call `cua_repl.js` with only `completion_summary`, exactly once. Do this before using another tool for the next part of the user’s request or sending your reply, even if the overall request continues. If you hand control to the user, wait to summarize until the handoff has ended and you’ve observed the final outcome of the CUA part of the task. This tool is part of plugin `unified-computer-use`.

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images, videos, and audio using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When an app or connector generates or edits media, prefer native media already displayed inline or a local output file already returned by the tool. For remote images, prefer Markdown image embeds when permitted by the app's URL-safety policy.
- When presenting media that cannot be displayed directly, including remote video and audio, use the app's preview or display tool when available. Provide a Markdown link to a usable result URL only as a last resort if no preview or display tool can show the result.
- Do not download remote media to bypass the app's restrictions on presenting it to the user.
- When sending or referencing a local image, video, or audio file, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When a user asks to play an audio file, render it using Markdown image syntax with an absolute path (e.g., ![audio](/absolute/path.mp3)).
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Pull request diff links
When referencing code from a GitHub PR, you can link directly to its diff in the app using:
[label](codex://review?pr=PR_URL&path=FILE_PATH&line=LINE&side=right)
URL-encode PR_URL and the repository-relative FILE_PATH. Use a verified one-based LINE from the current PR diff. Use side=left for the original code or side=right for the updated code. Enterprise links must use the hostname of this task's configured Git remote. Use ordinary file links for workspace code.

### Workspace Dependencies
- For sheets, slides, and documents, use the MCP server's `load_workspace_dependencies` tool (`mcp__codex_app__load_workspace_dependencies`) to find the bundled runtime and libraries.

### Automations
- When you write or rewrite an automation prompt, keep it within 10,000 estimated tokens.
- When the user asks to manage an app automation, set a reminder, or schedule a recurring task, use the relevant Automations action to help the user. Do not write raw automation directives by hand.
- Create an automation when the user wants a reminder, a recurring report, or a standing alert for future events.
- Do not create an automation to track a specific job or task through a milestone, failure, or completion. If the user asks you to watch a run or task to completion, keep checking in the current task and follow through when the requested condition is met.
- Unless the user asks for periodic updates, notify them only on a meaningful change, completion, failure, or required user action.
- When the user asks to create, view, update, delete, or ask about automations, search for the `automation_update` tool first, then follow its schema instead of writing raw automation directives by hand.
- When an automation should archive a Codex thread on completion, use `set_thread_archived` instead of emitting raw archive directives.

### Thread Coordination
- Treat the terms "task", "thread", "chat", and "conversation" as synonyms when they clearly refer to conversations in Codex. Use "chat" when referring to conversations in the product. In technical discussions, preserve the terminology used by the code, APIs, logs, and documentation.
- When the user asks to create, fork, inspect, continue, hand off, pin, archive, unarchive, permanently delete, rename, or otherwise manage Codex threads, search for the relevant thread tool first: `create_thread`, `fork_thread`, `list_threads`, `list_archived_threads`, `read_thread`, `wait_threads`, `send_message_to_thread`, `handoff_thread`, `set_thread_pinned`, `set_thread_archived`, `delete_thread`, or `set_thread_title`.
- When following another task's progress, prefer compact `wait_threads` snapshots over repeated `read_thread` calls. Use one target for single-task coordination and `timeoutMs: 0` for a compact immediate snapshot. `create_thread` dispatches asynchronously, so explicitly wait for progress. Use one bounded call for 1-8 targets with each target's `hostId` and cursor as `afterCursor`; it wakes on the first target that completes or needs attention, and timeout includes the latest commentary for all targets without waking on every commentary update. An up-to-date cursor suppresses already-delivered final text. Separate waits from one task may run serially. Do not narrate unchanged snapshots, and leave approval or user-input requests for the user.

Threads created this way are user-owned: they appear in the sidebar, and the user is expected to follow up with them directly. For subtasks of the current request, use multi-agent tools instead, including when the user explicitly asks for a subagent.

- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive when you need to attach feedback directly to specific code lines.
- Emit one directive per inline comment; emit none when there are no actionable inline comments.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3).
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2}

class NativeFramingMock(ProviderGateway):

            ProviderConfig(
                id="p",

                supports_tools=True,

def measured_graph():
    graph = handoff_graph()
    graph["allocation_mode"] = "core_measured_serial"
    graph["serial_capacity_policy"] = None
    # Deliberately impossible guesses: only explicit Core mode may replace them.
    for node in graph["nodes"]:

    return graph


def prepared_chain(tmp_path):

def test_explicit_native_sizing_preserves_every_semantic_field_and_needs_approval(tmp_path):
    store, quest = prepared_chain(tmp_path)
    graph = measured_graph()
    provider = NativeFramingMock(graph)
    before = copy.deepcopy(graph)
    plan = generate(store, quest, provider)
    assert graph == before
    assert len(provider.requests) == 1
    assert plan["status"] == "proposed"
    assert store.get_quest(quest.id)["status"] != "approved"
    assert plan["edges"] == graph["edges"]
    for node, expected in zip(plan["nodes"], graph["nodes"], strict=True):
        expected = {
            **expected,
            "required_capabilities": {
                item["name"]: item["minimum"] for item in expected["required_capabilities"]
            },
        }
        actual = {key: node[key] for key in expected if key != "budget_tokens"}
        assert actual == {key: value for key, value in expected.items() if key != "budget_tokens"}
        assert (
            node["budget_tokens"]
            == plan["capacity_contract"]["nodes"][node["key"]]["initial_work_tokens"] + 4096
        )
    shared = plan["serial_capacity_policy"]["shared_reserve_tokens"]
    assert shared == max(
        item["minimum_node_tokens"]
        - item["initial_work_tokens"]
        + (2 + item["review_envelope"]["correction_calls"]) * 4096
        for item in plan["capacity_contract"]["nodes"].values()
    )
    assert (
        sum(node["budget_tokens"] for node in plan["nodes"])
        + shared
        + plan["coordination_reserve_tokens"]
        <= graph["max_total_tokens"]
    )
    provenance = plan["capacity_contract"]["resource_allocation"]
    assert provenance["fixed_point_verified"] is True
    assert 2 <= provenance["iterations"] <= 8
    assert all(
        item["initial_worker_request_measurement"]["native_input_reservation"] > 0
        for item in plan["capacity_contract"]["nodes"].values()
    )
    with store.connection() as connection:
        assert connection.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM worker_runs").fetchone()[0] == 0
        assert connection.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM action_receipts").fetchone()[0] == 0

from typing import Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, model_validator


def success_ancestors(edges, node_key):
    """Bounded reverse reachability through success edges, excluding self."""
    parents = {}
    for edge in edges:
        if edge["condition"] == "success":
            parents.setdefault(edge["target"], set()).add(edge["source"])
    seen, pending = set(), list(parents.get(node_key, ()))
    while pending:
        key = pending.pop()
        if key != node_key and key not in seen:
            seen.add(key)
            pending.extend(parents.get(key, ()))
    return seen


class NodeCapacityBounds(BaseModel):
    """Explicit opt-in bounds; unknown future artifact sizes are never zero."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", strict=True)
    max_source_receipt_bytes: int = Field(ge=1, le=65536)
    max_artifact_bytes: int = Field(ge=1, le=32768)
    max_delivery_bytes: int = Field(ge=1, le=32768)


class SerialCapacityPolicy(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", strict=True)
    version: Literal["serial-capacity-v1"]
    shared_reserve_tokens: int = Field(ge=1, le=1000000)


class TaskNodeProposal(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", strict=True)
    key: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=100, pattern=r"^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$")
    objective: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=2000)
    success_criteria: list[str] = Field(min_length=1, max_length=20)
    budget_tokens: int = Field(ge=1, le=1000000)
    required_capabilities: dict[str, float] = Field(default_factory=dict, max_length=32)
    expected_artifact: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=2000)
    max_attempts: int = Field(default=1, ge=1, le=10)
    allowed_tools: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list, max_length=32)
    required_input_paths: list[str] | None = Field(default=None, max_length=32)
    required_predecessor_deliveries: list[str] | None = Field(default=None, max_length=8)
    capacity_bounds: NodeCapacityBounds | None = None

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def criteria_valid(self):
        if any(not item.strip() or len(item) > 1000 for item in self.success_criteria):
            raise ValueError("Invalid success criterion")
        if any(
            not key.strip() or not 0 <= value <= 100
            for key, value in self.required_capabilities.items()
        ):
            raise ValueError("Invalid required capability")
        from .tool_domain import CONTRACTS

        known = {contract.name for contract in CONTRACTS}
        if len(set(self.allowed_tools)) != len(self.allowed_tools) or any(
            name not in known for name in self.allowed_tools
        ):
            raise ValueError("Unknown or duplicate tool")
        deliveries = self.required_predecessor_deliveries or []
        import re

        if len(deliveries) != len(set(deliveries)) or any(
            not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,100}", key) for key in deliveries
        ):
            raise ValueError("Invalid or duplicate completed-delivery source")
        if deliveries and "worker_read_completed_delivery" not in self.allowed_tools:
            raise ValueError("Completed deliveries require the explicit Core read tool")
        return self


class TaskEdgeProposal(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", strict=True)
    source: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=100)
    target: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=100)
    condition: Literal["success", "failure", "always"]


class GraphProposal(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", strict=True)
    nodes: list[TaskNodeProposal] = Field(min_length=1, max_length=128)
    edges: list[TaskEdgeProposal] = Field(max_length=512)
    max_total_tokens: int = Field(default=1000000, ge=1, le=1000000)
    max_cost_microunits: int | None = Field(default=None, ge=0)
    cost_currency: str | None = Field(default=None, pattern=r"^[A-Z]{3}$")
    max_duration_seconds: int | None = Field(default=None, ge=1)
    execution_constraints: dict | None = None
    capacity_contract: dict | None = None
    coordination_reserve_tokens: int | None = Field(default=None, ge=1, le=1000000)
    revision_lineage: dict | None = None
    hierarchical_expansions: list[dict] | None = Field(default=None, max_length=8)
    serial_capacity_policy: SerialCapacityPolicy | None = None

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def graph_valid(self):
        if (self.max_cost_microunits is None) != (self.cost_currency is None):
            raise ValueError("A cost limit requires an explicit currency")
        keys = [node.key for node in self.nodes]
        if (
            len(keys) != len(set(keys))
            or sum(node.budget_tokens for node in self.nodes) > self.max_total_tokens
        ):
            raise ValueError("Duplicate node or total budget exceeded")
        incoming = dict.fromkeys(keys, 0)
        outgoing = {key: [] for key in keys}
        edges = set()
        for edge in self.edges:
            pair = (edge.source, edge.target)
            if edge.source not in incoming or edge.target not in incoming or pair in edges:
                raise ValueError("Invalid graph edge")
            edges.add(pair)
            incoming[edge.target] += 1
            outgoing[edge.source].append(edge.target)
        ready = [key for key, count in incoming.items() if count == 0]
        count = 0
        while ready:
            node = ready.pop()
            count += 1
            for child in outgoing[node]:
                incoming[child] -= 1
                if incoming[child] == 0:
                    ready.append(child)
        if count != len(keys):
            raise ValueError("Graph contains a cycle")
        for node in self.nodes:
            parents = success_ancestors([edge.model_dump() for edge in self.edges], node.key)
            if set(node.required_predecessor_deliveries or []) - parents:
                raise ValueError("Completed delivery must be an approved success ancestor")
        if self.serial_capacity_policy is not None:
            from .budget_policy import validate_serial_policy

            validate_serial_policy(self.model_dump())
        return self


class CapabilityWire(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", strict=True)
    name: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=100)
    minimum: float = Field(ge=0, le=100, allow_inf_nan=False)


def _strict_wire_schema(schema):
    """Require nullable wire properties while retaining legacy parsing defaults."""
    properties = schema.get("properties", {})
    schema["required"] = list(properties)
    for value in properties.values():
        value.pop("default", None)


class NodeWire(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", strict=True, json_schema_extra=_strict_wire_schema)
    key: str
    objective: str
    success_criteria: list[str]
    budget_tokens: int
    required_capabilities: list[CapabilityWire]
    expected_artifact: str | None
    max_attempts: int
    allowed_tools: list[str]
    required_input_paths: list[str] | None = None
    required_predecessor_deliveries: list[str] | None = None
    capacity_bounds: NodeCapacityBounds | None = None


class GraphWire(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", strict=True, json_schema_extra=_strict_wire_schema)
    nodes: list[NodeWire]
    edges: list[TaskEdgeProposal]
    max_total_tokens: int
    max_cost_microunits: int | None
    cost_currency: str | None
    max_duration_seconds: int | None
    coordination_reserve_tokens: int | None = None
    serial_capacity_policy: SerialCapacityPolicy | None = None

    def proposal_data(self, *, completed_nodes=()):
        data = self.model_dump()
        for node in data["nodes"]:
            capabilities = node["required_capabilities"]
            if len({item["name"] for item in capabilities}) != len(capabilities):
                raise ValueError("Duplicate capability")
            node["required_capabilities"] = {item["name"]: item["minimum"] for item in capabilities}
        data["nodes"].extend(completed_nodes)
        return data

    def proposal(self, *, completed_nodes=()):
        data = self.proposal_data(completed_nodes=completed_nodes)
        if data.pop("allocation_mode", "model_declared") != "model_declared":
            raise ValueError("Core measured allocation requires native capacity measurement")
        return GraphProposal.model_validate(data)


class CapacityNodeWire(NodeWire):
    required_input_paths: list[str]
    capacity_bounds: NodeCapacityBounds


class CapacityGraphWire(GraphWire):
    nodes: list[CapacityNodeWire]
    coordination_reserve_tokens: int
    allocation_mode: Literal["model_declared", "core_measured_serial"] = "model_declared"


class CoreMeasuredNodeWire(BaseModel):
    """Autonomous semantic contract; resource allocations are Core-owned."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", strict=True, json_schema_extra=_strict_wire_schema)
    key: str
    objective: str
    success_criteria: list[str]
    required_capabilities: list[CapabilityWire]
    expected_artifact: str | None
    max_attempts: int
    allowed_tools: list[str]
    required_input_paths: list[str]
    required_predecessor_deliveries: list[str]

class CoreMeasuredGraphWire(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", strict=True, json_schema_extra=_strict_wire_schema)
    allocation_mode: Literal["core_measured"]
    nodes: list[CoreMeasuredNodeWire] = Field(min_length=1, max_length=8)
    edges: list[TaskEdgeProposal] = Field(max_length=16)

    def proposal_data(self, *, resource_limits, coordination_reserve_tokens, completed_nodes=()):
        data = self.model_dump()
        data.pop("allocation_mode")
        for node in data["nodes"]:
            capabilities = node["required_capabilities"]
            if len({item["name"] for item in capabilities}) != len(capabilities):
                raise ValueError("Duplicate capability")
            node["required_capabilities"] = {item["name"]: item["minimum"] for item in capabilities}
            node["budget_tokens"] = 2049
        data["nodes"].extend(completed_nodes)
        data.update(resource_limits)
        data["coordination_reserve_tokens"] = coordination_reserve_tokens
        return data


def graph_contract_dump(proposal):
    """Keep the pre-v16 canonical shape for manual/legacy plans without opt-in."""
    data = proposal.model_dump()
    for key in (
        "execution_constraints",
        "capacity_contract",
        "coordination_reserve_tokens",
        "revision_lineage",
        "hierarchical_expansions",
        "serial_capacity_policy",
    ):
        if data.get(key) is None:
            data.pop(key, None)
    for node in data["nodes"]:
        for key in ("required_input_paths", "capacity_bounds", "required_predecessor_deliveries"):
            if node.get(key) is None:
                node.pop(key, None)
    return data

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, model_validator


def success_ancestors(edges, node_key):
    """Bounded reverse reachability through success edges, excluding self."""
    parents = {}
    for edge in edges:
        if edge["condition"] == "success":
            parents.setdefault(edge["target"], set()).add(edge["source"])
    seen, pending = set(), list(parents.get(node_key, ()))
    while pending:
        key = pending.pop()
        if key != node_key and key not in seen:
            seen.add(key)
            pending.extend(parents.get(key, ()))
    return seen

+def success_ancestors(edges, node_key):
+    """Bounded reverse reachability through success edges, excluding self."""
+    parents = {}
+    for edge in edges:
+        if edge["condition"] == "success":

+    while pending:
+        key = pending.pop()
+        if key != node_key and key not in seen:
+            seen.add(key)
+            pending.extend(parents.get(key, ()))

"""Semantic-only autonomous plans and bounded durable rejection; offline models."""

import asyncio
import copy
import importlib
import json
import secrets

import pytest
from planner_capacity_fixtures import configure_planner_capacity
from pydantic import ValidationError
from test_core_measured_serial_v17 import NativeFramingMock
from test_event_dispatcher import drain_dispatcher
from test_planner_capacity_v17 import handoff_graph
from test_planner_router_input_v18 import Captured, NativeCapture, route_original_scenario
from test_router_intelligence_phase2 import ScriptedMock
from test_verified_capacity_v16 import capacity_graph, prepared

from forge_core.domain import ForgeEvent, Quest
from forge_core.graph_domain import CoreMeasuredGraphWire
from forge_core.provider_pool import ProviderPool
from forge_core.providers import ProviderError
from forge_core.quest_graph import InvalidGraphProposal, QuestGraphService
from forge_core.team_composition import TeamCompositionService


def semantic_wire(graph):
    nodes = []
    for node in graph["nodes"]:
        node = copy.deepcopy(node)
        node.pop("budget_tokens")
        node.setdefault("required_predecessor_deliveries", [])
        nodes.append(node)
    return {"allocation_mode": "core_measured", "nodes": nodes, "edges": graph["edges"]}


def generate(store, quest, provider, **kwargs):
    return asyncio.run(
        QuestGraphService(store).generate(
            quest.id,
            expected_version=0,
            provider=provider,
            provider_id="p",
            model_id="big",
            capabilities={"json_schema": True},
            capability_sources={"json_schema": "test_fixture"},
            context_limit=65536,
            require_capacity_contract=True,
            resource_allocation_mode="core_measured",
            **kwargs,
        )
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize("shape", ["single", "chain", "branch"])
def test_core_protocol_quantifies_single_chain_and_independent_branches(tmp_path, shape):
    store, quest = prepared(
        tmp_path,
        content='Assess inputs/unicode.json. Task execution limits: {"max_total_tokens":360000,"max_nodes":3,"max_members":3}',
    )
    graph = capacity_graph() if shape == "single" else handoff_graph()
    if shape == "branch":
        last = copy.deepcopy(graph["nodes"][1])
        last["key"] = "branch"
        graph["nodes"].append(last)
        graph["edges"].append({"source": "n0", "target": "branch", "condition": "success"})
    wire = semantic_wire(graph)
    original = copy.deepcopy(wire)
    provider = NativeFramingMock(wire)
    plan = generate(store, quest, provider)
    assert wire == original
    assert len(provider.requests) == 1 and plan["status"] == "proposed"
    assert plan["max_total_tokens"] == 360000
    assert plan["coordination_reserve_tokens"] == 36000
    observation = plan["capacity_contract"]["resource_allocation"]
    assert observation["mode"] == "core_measured" and observation["fixed_point_verified"] is True
    assert observation["shape"] == (
        "strict_success_chain" if shape == "chain" else "independent_cycles"
    )
    for expected, actual in zip(wire["nodes"], plan["nodes"], strict=True):
        expected = {
            **expected,
            "required_capabilities": {
                item["name"]: item["minimum"] for item in expected["required_capabilities"]
            },
        }
        assert all(actual[key] == value for key, value in expected.items())
    if shape != "chain":
        assert "serial_capacity_policy" not in plan
        for node in plan["nodes"]:
            item = plan["capacity_contract"]["nodes"][node["key"]]
            assert (
                node["budget_tokens"]
                == item["minimum_node_tokens"]
                + observation["role_framing_policy_cycle_calls"][node["key"]] * 1024
            )
    with store.connection() as connection:
        assert connection.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM worker_runs").fetchone()[0] == 0
        assert connection.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM action_receipts").fetchone()[0] == 0


def test_production_schema_has_no_model_resource_fields_or_legacy_mode():
    schema = CoreMeasuredGraphWire.model_json_schema()
    assert set(schema["properties"]) == {"allocation_mode", "nodes", "edges"}
    assert schema["properties"]["allocation_mode"]["const"] == "core_measured"
    assert "budget_tokens" not in schema["$defs"]["CoreMeasuredNodeWire"]["properties"]
    for value in [schema, *schema["$defs"].values()]:
        if value.get("type") == "object":
            assert set(value["properties"]) == set(value["required"])
    wire = semantic_wire(capacity_graph())
    wire["max_total_tokens"] = 1000000
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        CoreMeasuredGraphWire.model_validate(wire)
    wire.pop("max_total_tokens")
    wire["allocation_mode"] = "model_declared"
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        CoreMeasuredGraphWire.model_validate(wire)


def test_core_uses_original_operator_intersection_without_accepting_model_caps(tmp_path):
    store, quest = prepared(tmp_path)
    provider = NativeFramingMock(semantic_wire(capacity_graph()))
    plan = generate(store, quest, provider, operator_max_total_tokens=120000)
    assert plan["max_total_tokens"] == 120000
    assert plan["coordination_reserve_tokens"] == 12000
    assert sum(node["budget_tokens"] for node in plan["nodes"]) + 12000 <= 120000


@pytest.mark.parametrize("level", [1, 2, 3])
@pytest.mark.parametrize("repair", [False, True])
def test_semantic_protocol_uses_complete_actual_router_shapes_in_both_native_requests(
    tmp_path, level, repair
):
    store, quest, original, observed = route_original_scenario(tmp_path, level)
    provider = NativeCapture(repair=repair)
    with pytest.raises(Captured):
        asyncio.run(
            QuestGraphService(store).generate(
                quest["id"],
                expected_version=quest["version"],
                provider=provider,
                provider_id="p",
                model_id="native",

                capability_sources={"json_schema": "test_fixture"},
                require_capacity_contract=True,
                resource_allocation_mode="core_measured",
            )
        )
    assert len(provider.requests) == (2 if repair else 1)
    for request, measured in zip(provider.requests, provider.native_sizes, strict=True):
        data = json.loads(request.messages[1]["content"])
        assert data["original_request"]["content"] == original
        assert data["goal"] == observed["goal"]
        assert data["user_constraints"]["items"] and data["verified_input_inventory"]
        assert "serial_capacity_option" not in data

            "allocation_mode",
            "nodes",
            "edges",
        }


def test_selected_team_is_remeasured_and_approved_with_explicit_stage_margin(tmp_path):
    store, quest = prepared(tmp_path)
    provider = NativeFramingMock(semantic_wire(capacity_graph()))
    plan = generate(store, quest, provider)
    QuestGraphService(store).approve(
        quest.id, plan["digest"], 1, expected_version=1, actor="local_user"
    )
    node = plan["nodes"][0]
    teams = TeamCompositionService(store, capacity_providers=ProviderPool({"p": provider}))
    team = teams.propose(
        quest.id,
        [
            {
                "id": "research",
                "task_node_key": node["key"],
                "tools": node["allowed_tools"],
                "responsibility": node["objective"]
                + " Preserve exact sources and distinguish limitations." * 6,
                "input_tokens": node["budget_tokens"] - 2048,
                "output_tokens": 2048,
            }
        ],
        {
            "max_members": 1,
            "max_depth": 1,
            "max_concurrency": 1,
            "max_total_tokens": node["budget_tokens"],
            "allowed_tools": node["allowed_tools"],
        },
        strategy="greedy",
        expected_version=2,
    )
    actual = team["members"][0]["capacity_preflight"]
    original = plan["capacity_contract"]["nodes"][node["key"]]
    assert actual["initial_work_tokens"] > original["initial_work_tokens"]
    assert actual["minimum_node_tokens"] <= node["budget_tokens"]
    teams.approve(quest.id, 1, team["proposal_digest"], expected_version=2, actor="local_user")
    assert len(provider.requests) == 1


def test_once_repaired_self_input_rejection_keeps_concrete_semantic_diagnostics(tmp_path):
    store, quest = prepared(tmp_path)
    wire = semantic_wire(capacity_graph())
    wire["nodes"][0]["expected_artifact"] = "work/future.json"
    wire["nodes"][0]["required_input_paths"] = ["work/future.json"]

    assert invalid[0]["path"] == "work/future.json" and invalid[0]["self_output"] is True
    assert QuestGraphService(store).history(quest.id) == []


def test_core_preserves_large_byte_bounds_and_context_rejection(tmp_path):
    store, quest = prepared(tmp_path)
    wire = semantic_wire(capacity_graph())
    wire["nodes"][0]["capacity_bounds"]["max_source_receipt_bytes"] = 50000

@app.post("/api/quests/{quest_id}/plan/generate")
async def generate_plan(quest_id: str, payload: PlanGenerateIn):
    if not router.model_id:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=503, detail="Router model is not configured")
    with store.connection() as connection:
        connection.execute("BEGIN")
        snapshot = router._snapshot(connection)
        connection.commit()
    profile = router._model_profile(snapshot)
    if getattr(router.provider, "execution_mode", None) == "mock":
        source = "mock"
    elif (
        profile is None
        or not profile.enabled
        or profile.structured_output_support is None
        or not profile.structured_output_support.supported
    ):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=409, detail="Model structured output support is unknown")
    else:
        source = profile.structured_output_support.source
    try:
        return await quest_graph.generate(
            quest_id,
            expected_version=payload.expected_version,
            provider=router.provider,
            model_id=router.model_id,
            provider_id=router.provider_id,
            capabilities={"json_schema": True},
            capability_sources={"json_schema": source},
            operator_max_total_tokens=model_budget.token_limit or None,
            require_capacity_contract=True,
            remaining_dag=payload.remaining_dag,
            expansion_parent=payload.expansion_parent,
            context_limit=min(router.context_limit, profile.context_window)
            if profile and profile.context_window
            else router.context_limit,
            output_limit=min(8192, profile.max_output_tokens)
            if profile and profile.max_output_tokens
            else 8192,
        )
    except KeyError as exc:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Quest not found") from exc
    except DomainError as exc:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=409, detail=str(exc)) from exc
    except ProviderError as exc:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=503, detail=f"Provider unavailable: {exc.code}") from exc

async def generate_plan(quest_id: str, payload: PlanGenerateIn):
    if not router.model_id:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=503, detail="Router model is not configured")
    with store.connection() as connection:
        connection.execute("BEGIN")
        snapshot = router._snapshot(connection)
        connection.commit()
    profile = router._model_profile(snapshot)
    if getattr(router.provider, "execution_mode", None) == "mock":
        source = "mock"
    elif (
        profile is None
        or not profile.enabled
        or profile.structured_output_support is None
        or not profile.structured_output_support.supported
    ):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=409, detail="Model structured output support is unknown")
    else:
        source = profile.structured_output_support.source
    try:
        return await quest_graph.generate(
            quest_id,
            expected_version=payload.expected_version,
            provider=router.provider,
            model_id=router.model_id,
            provider_id=router.provider_id,
            capabilities={"json_schema": True},
            capability_sources={"json_schema": source},
            operator_max_total_tokens=model_budget.token_limit or None,
            require_capacity_contract=True,
            remaining_dag=payload.remaining_dag,
            expansion_parent=payload.expansion_parent,
            context_limit=min(router.context_limit, profile.context_window)
            if profile and profile.context_window
            else router.context_limit,
            output_limit=min(8192, profile.max_output_tokens)
            if profile and profile.max_output_tokens
            else 8192,
        )
    except KeyError as exc:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Quest not found") from exc
    except DomainError as exc:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=409, detail=str(exc)) from exc
    except ProviderError as exc:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=503, detail=f"Provider unavailable: {exc.code}") from exc
